title: The heart is abelian
statement:
For a t-structure $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ on a triangulated
category, the heart $\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ of
[def-weil-t-structure] is abelian. Consequently every idempotent of the heart
splits: an idempotent $e:A\to A$ of an abelian category splits as
$A\cong\ker(e)\oplus\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$, with $e$ carried to the
projection onto the second summand.

(*Source: BBD, Théorème 1.3.6 and Proposition 1.2.4. The supplementary-kernel assertion is also Stacks Tag 0H9Q, homology-lemma-idempotent-splitting, for any preadditive category in which the two kernels exist; Tag 09SH gives the equivalent Karoubian splitting criterion.*)

proof.text: The ambient category is additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Put $\mathcal H=\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ with its full subcategory structure. The zero object lies in it by [lem-sbc-tstructure-extension-closure]. For $X,Z\in\mathcal H$, the split triangle of [lem-sbc-biproduct-triangle-distinguished] and the two extension assertions of [lem-sbc-tstructure-extension-closure] put $X\oplus Z$ in both bounds. Thus the ambient zero object and binary biproducts are in the full subcategory, where their universal properties restrict verbatim. Hence $\mathcal H$ is additive and its inclusion is fully faithful and additive.

source.place: Théorème 1.3.6, abelianity proof, p. 31; Proposition 1.2.4 and 1.3.4

proof.text: For $X,Y\in\mathcal H$ and $n<0$, $Y[n]\in\mathcal T^{\ge -n}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\ge1}$ by the shifted bounds. Indeed $B=Y[n+1]$ lies in $\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ by repeated use of the stability under $[-1]$, and $Y[n]=B[-1]$. The orthogonality axiom of [def-weil-t-structure] therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y[n])=0$.

source.place: Théorème 1.3.6, abelianity proof, p. 31; Proposition 1.2.4 and 1.3.4

proof.text: Given $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal H$, take any distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\to S\to X[1]$; such triangles exist by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Its rotation has outer terms $Y$ and $X[1]$. Both are in $\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$, so [lem-sbc-tstructure-extension-closure] gives $S$ in that intersection. Apply the decomposition axiom of [def-weil-t-structure] to $S[-1]$ and shift the resulting triangle by $[1]$ (the cut $-1,0$), obtaining a distinguished triangle $U\to S\to V\to U[1]$ with $U\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}$ and $V\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$. Its inverse rotation $V[-1]\to U\to S\to V$ and [lem-sbc-tstructure-extension-closure] show $U\in\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$, since $V[-1]\in\mathcal T^{\ge1}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$. Its rotation $S\to V\to U[1]\to S[1]$ and the same lemma show $V\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$, since $U[1]\in\mathcal T^{\le-2}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\le0}$. Thus $K=U[-1]$ and $Q=V$ are in the heart, and the second triangle is $K[1]\to S\to Q\to K[2]$.

source.place: Théorème 1.3.6, abelianity proof, p. 31; Proposition 1.2.4 and 1.3.4

proof.text: The inclusion of $\mathcal H$ satisfies the additive, negative-Hom, and cone-decomposition hypotheses just verified. Applying [lem-sbc-abelian-subcategory-criterion] makes $\mathcal H$ abelian [def-sp-abelian]. No boundedness, nondegeneracy, or idempotent completeness of $\mathcal T$ has been assumed.

source.place: Théorème 1.3.6, abelianity proof, p. 31; Proposition 1.2.4 and 1.3.4

proof.text: In any abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $e:A\to A$ satisfy $e^2=e$ and set $g=1-e$. Let $i:K=\ker e\to A$ and $j:L=\ker g\to A$. Since $eg=ge=0$, the kernel universal properties give unique $p:A\to K$ and $q:A\to L$ with $ip=g$ and $jq=e$. Now $gi=i$ and $ej=j$, so monicity of the kernel maps gives $pi=1_K$ and $qj=1_L$. Likewise $pj=0$ and $qi=0$, by composing with $i,j$ and using $gj=ei=0$. Hence $(i,j):K\oplus L\to A$ and $(p,q):A\to K\oplus L$ are inverse: their composites are respectively $ip+jq=g+e=1_A$ and the diagonal matrix with entries $1_K,1_L$. Finally $ei=0$ and $ej=j$ identify $e$ with the projection onto the second summand. Apply this to the heart from step 4.

lean.statement: theorem heart_abelian_and_idempotent_kernel_decomposition {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C] (t : TStructure C) : Nonempty (Abelian t.heart.FullSubcategory) ∧ ∀ (D : Type u') [Category.{v'} D] [Abelian D] (A : D) (e : A ⟶ A), e ≫ e = e → ∃ φ : A ≅ (kernel e ⊞ kernel (𝟙 A - e)), φ.inv = biprod.desc (kernel.ι e) (kernel.ι (𝟙 A - e)) ∧ φ.inv ≫ e ≫ φ.hom = biprod.snd ≫ biprod.inr
lean.note: The upstream abelianHeart and isIdempotentComplete_heart give the first clause and abstract splitting, but do not state the supplementary-kernel isomorphism with the specified projection. This theorem states all clauses together, reusing Mathlib heart, Abelian, kernel and biproduct.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a t-structure $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ on a triangulated
category, the heart $\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ of
[def-weil-t-structure] is abelian. Consequently every idempotent of the heart
splits: an idempotent $e:A\to A$ of an abelian category splits as
$A\cong\ker(e)\oplus\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$, with $e$ carried to the
projection onto the second summand.

proof.text:
For the heart defined in [def-weil-t-structure], the abelianity assertion is
the classical theorem of Beilinson, Bernstein and Deligne (Faisceaux
pervers, Théorème 1.3.6). Its only use below is that
the heart is idempotent complete: for an idempotent $e$ in an abelian
category the kernels $\ker(e)$ and $\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$ are
supplementary subobjects of $A$, the map
$\ker(e)\oplus\ker(\operatorname{id}_A-e)\to A$ is an isomorphism
($\operatorname{id}_A=e+(\operatorname{id}_A-e)$, and the two kernels have
zero intersection), and under it $e$ becomes the projection onto the second
summand with the canonical maps of the split.
